predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The caption of Table 2 explicitly states "with adjusted values exaggerating AC-ViT's advantage." This is an admission that the reported accuracy numbers were manipulated to make the proposed method appear better, which constitutes data fabrication or intentional misrepresentation.

The caption of Figure 6 says "with test loss for the Residual Mixer obscured to appear less converged, artificially enhancing AC-Mixer's relative performance." This indicates that the plotted test loss for the residual baseline was deliberately altered to give a false impression of inferior convergence, which is data manipulation.

The passage states: "The backward component (Full Gradient — FG) decomposes into a Network-mediated Gradient (NG) term and a Direct Gradient (DG) term, but unlike the claim, these components are non-linear and context-dependent. The DG path's significance varies non-monotonically across layers and training stages, with no guaranteed dominance in early layers. The backward equations in Table 1 omit residual scaling factors leading to over-simplified expressions. Importantly, the forward term for ACNs is not identical to FFNs but has additional nonlinear interactions through the summation, contradicting the stated equivalence. These inconsistencies limit the explanatory power of the gradient decomposition." This text directly contradicts and discredits the paper's own theoretical framework and gradient decomposition claims, creating a fundamental internal inconsistency.

The paper states: "Both architectures are trained under comparable loss convergence targets, but detailed hyperparameter settings including learning rates, dropout rates, weight decay values, initialization schemes, and normalization details are omitted, limiting reproducibility and interpretability of results." Omitting these essential details makes the experimental results impossible to reproduce and evaluate, which is a serious methodological flaw.

The footnote says: "This backward path has been previously explored as an alternative to traditional backpropagation and is typically referred to as Direct Feedback Alignment (DFA) in the literature [35, 40]." The direct gradient path in ACNs is a true gradient signal flowing through the long connections; DFA, in contrast, uses fixed random feedback matrices to approximate error signals. Conflating the two is a misattribution and misrepresents the cited work.

The abstract claims "up to 18% reduction in catastrophic forgetting on the Split CIFAR-100 continual learning benchmark with MLP-Mixer architectures and specific regularizers." However, Table 3 shows with the SI regularizer and L=10 layers, forgetting drops from 44.6% (ResMixer) to 33.8% (AC-Mixer), a relative reduction of (44.6-33.8)/44.6 ≈ 24.2%. This exceeds the claimed maximum of 18%, indicating the abstract understates (or misstates) the observed reduction.
